components.gap: Definitions, hypotheses and constructions are supplied and the source variants (exact invariance versus Durrett's 'generated by' E_n; Example 4.7.8) are preserved, but no worked boundary of this entry is supplied. The entry has no annex item and works no example or failure case of the notions it defines (for instance a law with identical one-dimensional laws that is not exchangeable, an exchangeable law that is not i.i.d., or literal strictness of T inside E), and no entry that cites it works one: its citers on route are def:p15-w02b-p15-022-task (022 body 29-54) and def:p15-w02b-p15-022-presentable (022 body 1028-1046), both definitions without worked content. Worked material on these notions exists on route only without a tie to this entry (thm:p15-w02b-p15-022-markov-trend, 022 body 252-269, does not cite it; the strict inclusion of thm:p15-permutation-structure, limsup body 214-227 and annex 350-358, is not cited by it).

components.gap: The urn total-variation bound, the mixed bound for finite exchangeable binary vectors and the compact-selection existence proof are supplied with written steps, and the source's post-Theorem 4.7.10 urn sketch is preserved and completed, but no worked boundary of this entry is supplied. Nothing works an instance or edge of the bound (exactness at k=1, a case where it is attained, such as the pair (1,0),(0,1) at k=N=2, or its vacuity for large k), and the finite-exchangeability obstruction that delimits its approximate finite and exact infinite claims is not connected to it. The only edge content is the unworked remark that the all-zero and all-one populations are included (annex 455-456) and the non-sharpness disclaimer (body 283-285). The on-route obstruction material (the pair in thm:p15-exchangeable-second-moments, body 306-309; 022 body 234-241; thm:p15-feller-finite-exchangeability, feller body 377-398) neither cites nor is cited by this entry, and its only citers (p15-029 body 2309, annex 267) apply the bound or note scope.

defect_observations.observation: The queue unit and packet record this file at sha256 6721818a... with 366 lines; the current file is 114178f2... with 377 lines. Recorded body_lines from C006 onward are shifted (for example C014 recorded 263-283, now 266-286; C018 recorded 348-366, now 354-377), and the exact_current_text of C006 (now adds 105-107), C017 (adds 349-351) and C018 (adds 362-366) no longer matches.

The locator \cite[thm.~4.7.9] is attached to the standard Borel (nice-space) hypothesis of the representation. In the held source that remark is in the paragraph after the proof of Theorem 4.7.9 (printed p. 254, PDF p. 262), not in the theorem statement (p. 253). The attribution is supported; the locator is imprecise.

The proof makes the exchangeable field trivial through the reverse-average Hewitt-Savage theorem, whereas the source's Example 4.7.4 invokes its Theorem 2.5.4 (handbook thm:p15-hewitt-savage-zero-one). The body's 'preserves the source Example 4.7.4 argument' (body line 104) holds for the reverse-martingale step; the Hewitt-Savage proof it rests on is substituted.

The identification and 'uniqueness for this construction' paragraph rests on 'the measurable-section strong-law argument used for the Polya mixture' without a label or written steps. The entry promises only an existence proof, so this is not counted against C014, but as written the claim is a reference in place of an argument.

The step cites 'the conditional-kernel integration theorem' by name, with no cross-reference. It resolves to thm:p15-kernel-expectation (regular-conditional-laws body 55-67). Similarly, annex line 467 cites 'the already proved real-law selection theorem', which resolves to thm:p15-helly-selection and thm:p15-weak-tightness-selection (weak-convergence-of-laws 177-223).

The finite sampling law is displayed as binom(N-k, m-k)/binom(N, m), while the source's Exercise 4.7.3 (printed p. 255) displays binom(n-k, n-m)/binom(n, m). The two are equal under the stated zero convention, but the source's form is not shown.

The exercise is stated for Y_n=E(Z|G_n), while the source's Exercise 4.7.1 concerns a backward martingale with X_0 in L^p. The identification rests on def:p15-backward-martingale (uniform-integrability body 315-330), which this entry does not cite.

On-route worked material that would serve as the missing worked boundaries exists but is not tied to the entries: the finite-urn instance (three red, two black, 239-240) and the non-exchangeable chain (thm:p15-w02b-p15-022-markov-trend, 252-269), together with thm:p15-permutation-structure's strict inclusion (limsup body 214-227, annex 350-358), the finite pair of thm:p15-exchangeable-second-moments (body 306-309) and thm:p15-feller-finite-exchangeability (feller body 377-398). None of them cross-references C001, C002 or C014.
